$comment: PLACEHOLDER RECORDS — the team directory with its employment block. Stands in for GET /api/v1/admin/team/members and GET /api/v1/admin/team/members/{id}. THIS IS THE ENDPOINT THAT DOES NOT EXIST YET AND BLOCKS EVERYTHING: `GET /admin/users/` returns only the members the signed-in admin created (getSelfCreatedUsersController), so there is no way to render a team-wide screen against the live API today. `memberId` is `AdminUserRow.id` — the SAME id Finance's SalaryAccount.memberId joins on, so it must stay a string of the server's own id and must not be re-minted here. `roles[]` is DISPLAY ONLY: roles are owned by the Roles module and read live from AdminOpsService.listRoles(); the copy here exists so the seed has something to put in a column. The employment block (designation, employmentType, joiningDate, reportsTo, workLocation, expectedHoursPerDay, dayStartsAt, graceMinutes, autoCloseAt) is the NEW half — it has no column anywhere on the server today and is what TeamProfile has to store. `reportsTo` is load-bearing: it is what scopes every read in this module (a senior sees their own reports, one level deep, TM-OD-01), so the API must return it and must scope server-side rather than expecting the client to filter.
$comment_asOf: The seed's own clock. Every elapsed time, late flag and 'today' on every screen is computed against this instant and never against the browser, so the fixture reads the same next month as it does now. Friday, mid-afternoon IST — chosen so the day is half-finished: some members working, one on a break, one who already closed, one absent and one who never clocked in.

members.name: Priya Iyer
members.$comment_dayStartsAt: Deliberately different from everyone else's 09:30. The late rule reads the MEMBER's own start time, not a company constant — a remote member on a agreed later start must not be marked late every single day, and a seed in which every row shares one threshold would never have caught it if the code read a constant.

members.name: N. Pillai
members.$comment_expectedHoursPerDay: Six, not eight. A contract member on shorter hours is why the day bar is measured against the MEMBER's expected hours rather than a company-wide 8 — otherwise every part-time row renders as permanently short.
members.$comment_roles: EMPTY ON PURPOSE. A member who can sign in and do nothing is the state the Members list exists to surface — the 'no role' count is the number that means work. A successful login never implies access.

$comment_department: WHICH PART OF THE COMPANY somebody belongs to. It is on the MEMBER and not on their salary account, because it is a fact about the person: a salary is a contract, a department is where they work, and the two change for different reasons and at different times. Finance reads it through `memberId` when a salary account is opened and never asks anybody to type it a second time — two people typing their own spelling produce Sales, sales and SALES in one payroll report. Blank is legal and groups as Unassigned in analytics. The server must NOT derive it from a designation, which does not partition into departments by itself: an Operations Manager and an Operations Executive share a department, a Sales Head and a Finance Admin do not, and no rule over job titles gets that right.
